property.name: colorbar_does_not_become_current_axes
property.claim: After mpu.colorbar returns, the newly created colorbar axes must not have become the current axes of the figure (gca is not hijacked).
property.quote: `mpu.colorbar` creates a new axes and hijacks `plt.gca()` - see if we can avoid this

pre_existing.relation: pre-existing: the same before the fix, and the failing call runs none of the fix's lines

survivors.description: Saves the first parent axes instead of the current axes, so the wrong axes is restored.
survivors.diff:
--- a/mplotutils/_colorbar.py
+++ b/mplotutils/_colorbar.py
@@ -215,3 +215,3 @@
     try:
-        original_ax = plt.gca()
+        original_ax = axs[0]
     except:
survivors.words: mplotutils/_colorbar.py:216: changing `        original_ax = plt.gca()` to `        original_ax = axs[0]` made no test fail; not compared with the fix: no compared function in its file

survivors.description: When there is no current axes, a restore target is set anyway instead of None, so the first axes becomes current.
survivors.diff:
--- a/mplotutils/_colorbar.py
+++ b/mplotutils/_colorbar.py
@@ -218,3 +218,3 @@
         # If there's no current axes, we'll set it back to the first provided axis
-        original_ax = None
+        original_ax = axs[0]
survivors.words: mplotutils/_colorbar.py:219: changing `        original_ax = None` to `        original_ax = axs[0]` made no test fail; not compared with the fix: no compared function in its file
